title: object spread enumerates a foreign value's own getters, so it invokes foreign code and keeps the panic case
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, "Foreign Boundary": "Calling an unannotated foreign runtime value MUST add the checked `panic` case, because JavaScript and TypeScript may throw, reject, or violate a declaration." This is the enumeration protocol rather than the iteration one: `{ ...x }` reads every own enumerable property, and a getter is arbitrary foreign code. 09-foreign-calls/foreign-property-read-needs-an-adapter already pins the getter read that a property-access node spells; this pins the one that no property-access node spells at all, which is why it was fail-open while that one was not.
